subject: Computer Networking
title: Bluetooth Basics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bluetooth Basics usable.

hook.text: Your headphones, keyboard, and smartwatch all talk to your phone wirelessly. They all use Bluetooth.

buildup.text: Bluetooth operates at 2.4 GHz over short range — typically under 10 meters. Low power is its defining feature.

discovery.text: Devices pair by exchanging keys. Once paired, they reconnect automatically whenever they're in range.

twist.text: Classic Bluetooth and BLE are different. BLE uses far less power and is designed for IoT sensors and wearables.

climax.text: Bluetooth 5 quadrupled the range and doubled the speed of BLE. The latest versions add direction finding too.

punchline.text: Bluetooth connects the things closest to you. Short range, big impact.

quiz.question: What is BLE designed for?
options: Low-power devices like sensors and wearables

details.summary: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology for connecting personal devices like headphones, keyboards, fitness trackers, and smartwatches. It operates in the 2.4 GHz band using frequency hopping to resist interference.
details.whyItMatters: Bluetooth connects more wireless devices than any other technology. BLE's ultra-low power consumption enabled the explosion of wearables, beacons, and IoT sensors.
takeaways: Bluetooth uses frequency hopping across 79 channels in 2.4 GHz
BLE extends battery life to years on a single coin cell
Bluetooth 5 increased range fourfold and speed twofold over 4.2

faq.question: What is the difference between Bluetooth Classic and BLE?
faq.answer: Bluetooth Classic supports continuous streaming for audio and file transfer with higher power consumption. BLE uses short bursts of communication with long sleep intervals, consuming a fraction of the power. Most modern devices support both.

faq.question: How does Bluetooth handle interference from Wi-Fi?
faq.answer: Both use 2.4 GHz but Bluetooth frequency-hops 1600 times per second across 79 channels, avoiding channels where interference is detected. Adaptive frequency hopping avoids Wi-Fi channels entirely. Colocated Bluetooth and Wi-Fi radios coordinate their transmissions to minimize mutual interference.
